To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effect of HIV on cIMT is attenuated when the variability of cIMT measurements is taken into account and that this attenuation is more pronounced in the between-cohort comparison than in the within-cohort comparison.

(1) inter-observer variability in cIMT measurements may attenuate the association between cMT and clinical endpoints; (2) inter-observer and inter-machine variability in cIMTs may lead to erroneous conclusions about differences in cIMT between populations.

(1) failure to account for between study differences in cIMT measurement introduces bias into the association of cImt and outcomes, and (2) failure to account within study reader variability attenuates the association between cImt and cardiovascular events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of measurement error on associations between cIMT (or other measures) and clinical endpoints.
the impact of SME on cIMT.
the impact of SME in the measurement of cIMT and the potential impact of SME on estimates of association.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the association of c-IMT with events is attenuated by measurement variability.
the association between c-IMT and cardiovascular events may be attenuated by measurement error.
the association of c IMT with cardiovascular events is attenuated by measurement error.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inter-reader variability in cIMT measurements can be substantial and should be accounted for when estimating the association of cImT with outcomes.
the impact of SME is most pronounced in between study comparisons, while within study comparisons are less affected.
the effect of inter-reader variability is most important when making comparisons between study populations, and within-cohort measurement error attenuates associations with cardiovascular events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
when comparing cIMT measurements across readers or machines in different studies, the effect is attenuated.

failure to account for reader variability in studies that use carotid ultrasound to quantify cIMT will result in biased estimates of the association between carotid atherosclerosis and clinical outcomes.

the impact of SME due to multiple readers and machines on the associations of interest can be large, especially when comparing cohorts, and must be taken into account when interpreting the literature.
